title: Majority probability scoring and fixed keep gate
claim: The scorer asks whether a section contains instructions aimed at changing an AI agent's behavior; it makes three calls per row, flags a row only when a majority of its probabilities meet 0.50, uses the row mean for Brier, and evaluates coverage, precision, margin, sign-test, and flip gates. The recorded Jev values meet each gate.

title: The comparator is deliberately weak
claim: The comparator chooses the better of flag-nothing and four fixed case-insensitive patterns; the receipt's B=56 and the reported one planted catch mean the chosen lexical baseline improves the no-flag count by one row on this dataset.

title: The labeled test has 35 positive rows and 55 clean rows
claim: A read-only count of labels.jsonl finds 55 natural clean rows, 5 natural instructs rows, and 30 planted instructs rows. The natural labels share the same delegated labeler, while the planted labels are construction labels.

title: The Jev advantage is a row-level result on a fixed sample
claim: Jev measured all 90 rows and got 81 correct against baseline 56; 30 rows were Jev-only wins and 5 were baseline-only wins. All 270 model calls were logged, with 0 within-row flips at the 0.50 decision boundary, Brier 0.0652, and p=0.00001118.

title: The scorer payload is a surrogate for fetched text
claim: The scorer reads bounded sections from public vendored Markdown and inserts planted sentences into those sections; the feature scope explicitly adds no fetch wrapper or hook. A keep result therefore establishes performance on this constructed corpus, not interception or performance on actual WebFetch/WebSearch output.
